definition: A spread trade that speculates on the natural gas price difference between two different time periods.
core_idea: Because gas demand varies seasonally, traders can bet on the relative price difference between a high-demand and a low-demand period without taking on outright market direction risk.
key_points: Time spreads speculate on the price difference between periods of high and low demand.
Example: buying winter gas and selling spring gas to bet on a colder-than-normal winter while removing exposure to the overall market direction.
relationships: Related to the seasonal shape of the forward curve
trading_implications: Lets traders express a seasonal-demand view (e.g., a cold winter) without outright market exposure.
